core_obligations: Reduce to an affine base (proof lines 18546-18555): for a proper f : X -> Y and an affine open covering Y = union Y_i, proving base change for the restrictions X_i -> Y_i implies it for f, because the higher direct images localise on the base; hence one may assume Y affine.

Apply Chow's lemma (proof lines 18557-18569): for affine Y and proper X -> Y, Chow's lemma gives a diagram with X' -> X proper surjective and X' -> P^n_Y an immersion; properness of X -> Y makes X' -> Y proper and hence X' -> P^n_Y a closed immersion, so X' -> X x_Y P^n_Y = P^n_X is a closed immersion.

Reduce to projections (proof lines 18571-18607): by the sandwich principle it suffices to prove base change for pi and for X' -> Y; both factor as a closed immersion followed by a projection P^n_S -> S, closed immersions are finite so the finite lemma applies, and the composition principle reduces the claim to the projections P^n_S -> S; a final application of the same three principles, using the explicit factorisation of the projection via the polynomial display, concludes that the statement for P^1_S -> S suffices.
proof_roadmap: Localise on an affine open covering of the base so that the base may be assumed affine.
Use Chow's lemma to replace the proper morphism by a closed immersion into a projective bundle together with a proper surjective morphism.
Apply the sandwich, finite and composition principles to reduce everything to the projections, and then to P^1 over the base.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is a reduction step for the proof of general proper base change: it shows that it suffices to know the statement for the projections P^1_S -> S (statement lines 18538-18543). The proof (proof lines 18545-18607) localises on the base, applies Chow's lemma to obtain a closed immersion of X' into a projective bundle together with the proper surjective pi, and uses the sandwich, finite and composition principles twice to reduce first to the projections P^n_S -> S and then, through the explicit factorisation using the polynomial display, to P^1_S -> S. H2: a chain of named reductions, each written out.
